# PLAN — iteration 5

## Current state assessment

Iteration 4 is the verified timing-feasible best: WNS and WHS are nonnegative, and its register-to-register WNS is 0.267 ns. Iterations 1, 2, and 4 were accepted; iteration 3 was rejected after setup regressed. The advisor trial also reports 0.267 ns, so it does not show an objective gain. Since both designs are timing-feasible, promotion requires a strictly higher register-to-register WNS at the same clock period.

## Hypothesis

For parameter pairs that are equal, exploiting the FIR’s symmetric taps may reduce four registered multipliers to four pair-sum multipliers and shorten the output accumulation, potentially improving register-to-register setup slack.

## Instruction for generator

Keep the `// @latency 1` annotation and change only the product-register and `y_out` accumulation pattern: for each pair `(C0,C7)`, `(C1,C6)`, `(C2,C5)`, and `(C3,C4)`, use a generate-time equality check to register the 32-bit truncated product of the corresponding signed 17-bit sample sum and coefficient. For any unequal coefficient pair, retain the independent 32-bit product registers and equivalent accumulation so every supported parameter value preserves behavior. Keep synchronous reset, registered outputs, and the existing cycle alignment; compare routed register-to-register WNS and all mandatory verification gates before considering promotion.
